subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should native iOS Siri/Shortcuts App Intent support be accepted, and which security/session boundary should it use for agent execution and spoken replies?
rationale: The implementation boundary affects credential exposure, unattended automation, session selection, delivery routing, and whether Siri bypasses existing paired-node controls.

options.title: Sponsor paired-node AppIntent design
options.body: Implement the feature in apps/ios using the authenticated paired Gateway/node session, explicit session behavior, local confirmation rules, and focused iOS proof before merge.

options.title: Use hooks as opt-in integration
options.body: Keep Siri/Shortcuts execution outside normal paired-node chat and require explicit hook token configuration, restricted session prefixes, and documented operator opt-in.

options.title: Keep Shortcuts workaround only
options.body: Do not add native AppIntent support until a maintainer wants to own the product and security surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor paired-node AppIntent design
recommendation.body: Implement the feature in apps/ios using the authenticated paired Gateway/node session, explicit session behavior, local confirmation rules, and focused iOS proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest combined history on AppIntents linkage, iOS agent-deep-link security, and iOS app ownership signals.
